channel.title: Columbia Journalism Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Columbia Journalism Review (cjr.org)

item.title: As US Bombs Iran, a Judge Rules on the Battle for Hearts and Minds
item.description: A federal court says Kari Lake didn’t have legal standing to gut federally funded broadcasters such as Voice of America and Radio Free Europe.

item.title: Inside the Legal Defense of Georgia Fort and Don Lemon
item.description: “You can look back at this last year and see that the administration’s attacks on the media are very much content-oriented,” Lemon’s lawyer said.

item.title: Why Economic Independence Is Not Enough
item.description: After a decade spent brainstorming business models, Europe’s newsrooms now confront legal and government pressure that shows money can’t fix everything.

item.title: On Standing Rock, Local News Is Teetering
item.description: “We are like living ghosts,” the editor of the Teton Times said.

item.title: Estefany Rodríguez in Limbo
item.description: Last week, a reporter in Nashville was detained by ICE. Officials claimed to have paperwork for her arrest, but her lawyers say it was warrantless—and retaliation for her reporting.

item.title: Cinematrix Is a Blockbuster
item.description: Inside New York’s addictive movie trivia game.

item.title: Are Prediction Markets Actually Good for Journalism?
item.description: Dustin Gouker, the author of a Substack about prediction markets, says the media could benefit from keeping an eye on Kalshi and Polymarket.

item.title: Lessons from an Early-Career Journalist
item.description: “I wouldn’t be getting this experience at a national publication, to be extensively following the hottest news story in the country.”

item.title: How Journalists Can Make AI Work for Them
item.description: A framework for newsrooms to use AI in ways that don’t sacrifice quality or lessen oversight.

item.title: The Role of Non-Journalism Civic Information
